blocks.text: Model evaluation checks how well a machine learning model performs. It measures the quality of the model's predictions on test data that was not used in training, which shows the model's strengths and weaknesses. Performance metrics are the measures used, and different metrics suit different problems.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: A model with high accuracy can still give wrong results in some cases; that is why measures such as precision and recall are also used.

items: TP (true positives): positive cases correctly predicted as positive.
TN (true negatives): negative cases correctly predicted as negative.
FP (false positives): negative cases wrongly predicted as positive.
FN (false negatives): positive cases wrongly predicted as negative (missed cases).

blocks.text: Accuracy is the share of all predictions that are correct, measured as a percentage: accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN). High accuracy means better performance. The error shows the incorrect predictions; the error rate is the opposite of accuracy. Accuracy alone can sometimes mislead, and balanced data gives better accuracy results, so error analysis is also used to find mistakes; both measures are important for evaluation.

items: Precision = TP / (TP + FP): of the cases predicted positive, how many really are positive. It measures correctness; high precision means fewer false results.
Recall = TP / (TP + FN): of the actual positive cases, how many were found. It measures completeness; high recall means few missed cases.

F1-score = 2 x (precision x recall) / (precision + recall): one score that balances precision and recall. It is especially useful when the data is unbalanced, and a higher F1-score means better performance.
